summary: Earth Pulse is an interactive 3D Earth platform designed to identify and understand long-term environmental changes using NASA Earth-observation data. Users can select geographical regions and investigate environmental variables such as 2-metre air temperature and precipitation. The platform uses NASA MERRA-2 datasets, with NASA GPM IMERG as an optional rainfall cross-check. Python-based statistical methods, including Linear Regression, Sen's Slope and the Mann–Kendall test, identify trend direction, magnitude and statistical significance. Interactive charts and AI-assisted explanations make scientific findings easier to understand.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Earth Pulse is an interactive 3D Earth platform that helps users investigate long-term environmental changes using NASA Earth-observation data. Users can explore the 3D globe, select geographical regions and examine environmental variables such as 2-metre air temperature and precipitation.

The platform uses NASA MERRA-2 historical atmospheric data, with NASA GPM IMERG as an optional precipitation comparison source. The selected data is processed using Python, and statistical techniques such as Linear Regression, Sen's Slope and the Mann–Kendall test are used to identify trends, measure their magnitude and assess statistical significance.

The results are presented through interactive maps, graphs, regional comparisons and AI-assisted explanations, helping users understand how environmental conditions change over time.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Makes complex NASA Earth science datasets easier to explore and understand.
  • Helps identify increasing and decreasing environmental trends.
  • Enables comparisons between different geographical regions.
  • Provides statistical evidence to support environmental observations.
  • Converts scientific data into understandable visualizations and explanations.
  • Encourages data-driven environmental awareness and learning.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our aim is to make Earth-system data more accessible, understandable and useful for students, researchers, educators and environmental enthusiasts. By transforming historical satellite and atmospheric data into meaningful visual insights, Earth Pulse encourages people to understand regional environmental changes and make evidence-based interpretations.

The project also promotes scientific curiosity, environmental awareness and the use of data analytics to investigate changes occurring across our planet.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software were used?

Programming languages:

  • Python – Data processing and statistical analysis.
  • JavaScript – Interactive web application development.

Frontend and visualization:

  • React.js and Vite – User interface.
  • react-globe.gl – Interactive 3D Earth visualization.
  • Leaflet – Geographical mapping.
  • Plotly – Interactive charts and graphs.

Backend and data processing:

  • FastAPI – Backend APIs.
  • Pandas and NumPy – Data processing.
  • Xarray – Handling scientific gridded datasets.
  • GeoPandas – Geographical data processing.
  • SciPy and pymannkendall – Statistical analysis.

NASA data sources:

  • NASA MERRA-2 – Historical atmospheric data.
  • NASA GPM IMERG – Precipitation data.
  • NASA Giovanni and Earthdata – Data access and preparation.

This is a software-based project, so no specialized hardware is required.

5. How is your project creative?

The creative aspect of Earth Pulse is the combination of interactive 3D Earth exploration, NASA scientific datasets, statistical trend detection and AI-assisted interpretation in one platform.

Instead of simply displaying environmental information, users become Earth System Trend Detectives. They can select a location, investigate environmental variables, discover patterns, compare regions and understand the scientific evidence behind the results.

The platform connects scientific analysis with an interactive experience, making Earth-system investigation more engaging and accessible.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered the following factors while designing the project:

  • Data reliability: Using authentic NASA datasets and maintaining their source information.
  • Scientific accuracy: Applying appropriate statistical methods and reporting uncertainty.
  • Usability: Creating a simple interface that users with different technical backgrounds can understand.
  • Performance: Selecting lightweight technologies suitable for a 24-hour development period.
  • Scalability: Designing the platform so additional environmental variables and datasets can be incorporated later.
  • Accessibility: Presenting complex scientific findings through interactive visualizations and simple explanations.
  • Reproducibility: Retaining dataset names, units, observation periods and analysis methods.
  • Responsible interpretation: Avoiding unsupported causal conclusions and ensuring AI explanations are based on calculated results.

Our vision: To transform complex Earth-observation data into meaningful discoveries and help everyone understand how our planet is changing.
